title: Structured-output resilience runbook: incremental constraints, token-sentinel heuristics, and rollback workflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational runbook and test plan for JSON-mode and constrained-decoding failures during streaming responses and interleaved tool/function calls. Focus on progressive constraint application, token-sentinel heuristics to detect truncation/corruption, recovery recipes for partial emits, and explicit rollback/partial-rollout flows for console and API routes.
background: We've observed partial-stream emits and schema corruption primarily in long-stream sessions with interleaved tool calls. Current mitigations (simple backoff + strict parser) cause high latency and customer-visible failures for real-time apps. This ticket captures a reproducible runbook, automated checks, and operational guidance for on-call engineers and SREs.
scope: Design and validate a deterministic set of tests and recovery steps for JSON-mode enforcement and constrained-decoding regressions across hosted and dedicated routes. Produce alerting/telemetry dashboards, canary gating rules, and an on-call rollback playbook. Exclude offline batch embedding jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook outlining detection heuristics for truncated/invalid JSON in streamed responses
Automated tests that simulate interleaved tool calls and validate constrained-decoder fallback behaviors
Playbook steps for safe canary rollback and emergency model variant fallback
Dashboards and alert rules that surface schema-violation rate by route/model/customer
A postmortem template and follow-up action list for any detected regression
test_plan: Create synthetic sessions with streaming length >= 4096 tokens and interleaved tool calls to reproduce corruption patterns
Inject adversarial token sequences that mimic partial JSON tokens (e.g., truncated escapes, broken arrays) and validate detector sensitivity
Run constrained-decoder with different backoff policies (strict reject, soft-relax, sentinel-insert) and record latency/quality tradeoffs
Simulate network interruption mid-stream and validate KV-cache recovery and reassembly logic
Cross-route canary: run new schema-enforcer on 1% of traffic with mirrored telemetry and automated alerting if schema-violation > 0.1%
rollback_procedures: Immediate: switch routing policy to last-known-good model variant via smart-routing control plane
Short-term: enable permissive constrained-decoding mode (soft-relax) on affected routes to reduce customer impact
Mid-term: redeploy streaming reassembly patch with increased tolerances behind canary gating
Communication: publish status to Console incidents with expected ETA and affected customers list
mitigation_steps: Token-sentinel heuristic: append/expect an explicit end-sentinel token for structured outputs and fail-fast if missing
Incremental constraints: progressively relax schemas for long streams (allow partial arrays, optional fields) and revalidate at end-of-stream
Prefetch KV-cache checkpoints at safe boundaries (N tokens) to reduce lost state on reconnect
Graceful truncation: on detected corruption, attempt to salvage last well-formed object and emit a 'truncated' flag
